skill.name: container-orchestration
skill.description: Container orchestration patterns for Dockerfiles, Docker Compose, Kubernetes manifests, Helm charts, and AWS ECS Fargate deployments.
skill.summary: Create and review container deployment assets across Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, and AWS ECS Fargate.
skill.author: 0xDarkMatter

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, Dockerfile templates, local health checks, and offline tests. Confirmed issues are insecure default or plaintext secret examples, a debug listener bound to all interfaces, and overbroad Kubernetes secret RBAC. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Default and plaintext secret values appear in container examples.
remediation.suggestion: Use non-secret placeholders, external secret references, or secret manager examples. Make production examples avoid committed credentials entirely.

remediation.issue: The Kubernetes RBAC example grants list access to secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Remove broad secret permissions, avoid list on secrets, and scope any required secret read with resourceNames or external secret injection.

remediation.issue: The debug container example listens on all interfaces.
remediation.suggestion: Bind debug tooling to localhost where possible, require an explicit debug profile, and warn users not to expose debug ports publicly.

remediation.issue: The build script can perform real Docker builds and registry pushes.
remediation.suggestion: Document dry-run-first usage and require user confirmation before running build or push commands in agent workflows.

content.user_title: Orchestrate Containers with Docker, Kubernetes, and ECS
content.value_statement: Teams often lose time translating container plans into deployable files. This skill gives Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, and ECS patterns for faster orchestration work.
actual_capabilities: Drafts multi-stage Dockerfile structures with non-root users, health checks, and runtime settings.
Provides Docker Compose layouts for application, database, cache, worker, and proxy services.
Shows Kubernetes Deployment, Service, Ingress, autoscaling, disruption budget, and network policy patterns.
Outlines Helm chart structure, values files, helper templates, deployment templates, and release commands.
Explains AWS ECS Fargate architecture, networking, IAM roles, secrets, scaling, observability, and deployment tooling.
Includes a Docker build and push helper script with a dry-run mode for review.
limitations: It does not connect to a live cluster or cloud account by itself.
Generated manifests still need review against current platform versions and organization policies.
Example secrets and default credentials must be replaced before any production use.
The build script can perform real Docker builds and registry pushes when run without dry-run mode.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Service Container
use_cases.description: Create a Dockerfile and Compose setup for a web service that needs a database and cache.

use_cases.title: Plan a Kubernetes Release
use_cases.description: Draft manifests for a production service with health probes, autoscaling, RBAC, and network policy.

use_cases.title: Choose an Orchestrator
use_cases.description: Compare ECS Fargate and Kubernetes for an AWS workload before choosing a deployment model.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Dockerfile
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production Dockerfile for a Python web API. Use a non-root user, dependency caching, and a health check. Explain each section briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Local Compose Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Docker Compose plan for an app, PostgreSQL, and Redis. Include volumes, health checks, environment variables, and safe local defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Design Kubernetes Manifests
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Kubernetes manifests for a stateless API. Include Deployment, Service, Ingress, HPA, PDB, probes, resource limits, and a NetworkPolicy.

prompt_templates.title: Compare ECS and Kubernetes
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare ECS Fargate and Kubernetes for an AWS service with private networking, secret injection, autoscaling, logging, and blue-green deployments.

output_examples.input: I need a production Dockerfile for a Python API.
output_examples.output: A staged implementation plan that names the base image, dependency layer, non-root user, health check, exposed port, and runtime command.

output_examples.input: I need Kubernetes files for a public web service.
output: A deployment plan with replicas, probes, resource requests, and security context.
A service and ingress plan with TLS notes and routing assumptions.
A review checklist for secrets, RBAC, and network policy.

output_examples.input: Should this workload use ECS Fargate or Kubernetes?
output_examples.output: A decision summary comparing operations effort, portability, AWS integration, networking, IAM, deployment tooling, and cost controls.

best_practices: Replace placeholder credentials with a secret manager or approved runtime secret source.
Review generated manifests with security, networking, and platform teams before deployment.
Use dry-run and template output modes before applying changes to clusters or registries.
anti_patterns: Do not copy example passwords or API keys into production manifests.
Do not expose debug ports or database ports without an explicit network boundary.
Do not grant broad secret access to application service accounts without a clear need.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy containers automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns, templates, and commands. Users must decide when to run deployment actions.

faq.question: Can it help with both Docker and Kubernetes?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Dockerfiles, Docker Compose, Kubernetes manifests, Helm charts, and ECS Fargate concepts.

faq.question: Does it replace official cloud documentation?
faq.answer: No. Users should verify current AWS, Kubernetes, Helm, and Docker behavior before production rollout.

faq.question: Are the examples production ready?
faq.answer: They are starting points. Users must replace secrets, tune resources, and review access controls.

faq.question: Does the script push images by default?
faq.answer: No. The script pushes only when the push option is supplied, but it can still build images.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
